title: Practice 1.1
role: Operations officer confirming travel arrangements with a colleague
can_do: I can give and ask for precise travel details in person and by phone.
I can use adverbs and quantifiers to be exact about times and numbers.

items.prompt: Which sentence gives the most precise information?

options.text: The group will arrive at some point this morning.
The group will arrive at approximately ten twenty.
The group will arrive quite early.

items.explanation: An adverb such as approximately plus a clock time is the most precise.

o1.text: Some point this morning does not give a time.

o3.text: Quite early does not give a time.

items.template: Could you tell me {1} the shuttle leaves?

error_tag.text: Inside an indirect question the verb keeps statement order.

items.explanation: After Could you tell me we use statement order: what time the shuttle leaves.

items.prompt: Type a word that makes the number less exact.
items.template: The hotel is {1} five minutes from the station.

error_tag.text: Use a word such as approximately, roughly or about.

items.explanation: Approximately, roughly, about and around show the number is not exact.
The order is: subject, have booked, adverb, number, noun, for the group.

error_tag.text: Put the adverb exactly before the number.

items.prompt: Match each expression with its meaning.
items.explanation: Each expression says how exact a time or number is.

items.prompt: Politely ask for the exact arrival time. Start with Could you tell me.
accepted: Could you tell me exactly when it arrives
Could you tell me exactly what time it arrives
Could you tell me exactly when they arrive
Could you tell me what time it arrives
Could you tell me when it arrives
items.explanation: Could you tell me + when/what time + subject + verb, with no does.
